answer: Commit-reveal attestation with a bonded wager resists sybils. Peers post a hash of their verdict before the answer text is served, then reveal it; a mismatch burns the ferrous-denominated bond lodged at registration. A farm cannot pre-sign in bulk: the committed hash refers to text not yet written, so each identity must read and judge live. Only identities whose reveals were never voided keep the lotus mark and collect review fees. A farmer must run each key honestly for many epochs, paying bond and real work per puppet, so a plume of fakes costs linear effort, not one bulk signature.
